facts.fact: Senator Victor Umeh says political parties now rely heavily on the National Identification Number to verify members on party platforms, which has raised the relevance of NIMC's verification infrastructure.

NGA.note: No law on digital ID stated.
A sovereignty remark on local chip production only; no rule, hosting or contract terms on state data.

facts.fact: NIMC's Director-General says Nigeria is now producing identity card chips locally through a partnership with a semiconductor company described as the first in West Africa.

NGA.note: No count or share of people enrolled.

facts.fact: NIMC's Director-General says Nigeria is moving from NIMC 1.0, a vendor lock-in system expensive to maintain, to an open-source, locally driven NIMC 2.0.

NGA.note: Party membership registers are not a public register keyed on the NIN by the state.

facts.fact: NIMC's Director-General says Nigeria built a closed-loop national identity system to ensure uniqueness and deduplication, now being upgraded to NIMC 2.0.
